 K-pop giants turn their backs on the Grammys.
 BTS and many leading entertainment companies have decided not to submit applications for the new Grammy Awards.
 Báo Thanh niên • 22/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 K-pop fans debate the Grammy boycott.
 The wave of protests against the Grammy Awards is showing signs of shifting. The anger of the fan community is no longer directed solely at the organizers (the National Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences), but is beginning to be directed towards K-pop groups that allegedly submitted entries. 
 BTS announced they will not be submitting an application for the new Grammy category.
 Photo: Reuters
 Although the organizers haven't officially announced the list, leaked information in the South Korean media has sparked heated debates. According to Koreatimes , many viewers are questioning whether their idols should be competing in a category considered discriminatory. Some even harshly called it a "racist award."
 Conversely, some fans argue that seeking Grammy nominations remains a practical step in an artist's career development.
 You may also like The controversy began in June when the Grammy organizers announced the introduction of a "Best Asian Pop Performance" category for the 69th Grammy Awards (to be held in February 2027). This award is for recordings using Asian languages. However, observers believe this is a ploy to relegate K-pop to a separate niche, instead of recognizing it in the main categories.
 According to Koreatimes , BTS was the first group to spark the boycott. On July 29, the group announced they would not be submitting an application and asserted that music should be received naturally, without being divided by geographical or language barriers. This decision came as a surprise because their album ARIRANG, released in March, was considered a strong contender.
 On October 1st, the organizers confirmed that this category would remain unchanged. CEO Harvey Mason Jr. stated that the majority of supporters within the Asian music community still hold significant influence. 
 JYP Entertainment has confirmed that Stray Kids are out of the running for the Grammy Awards' new category.
 Photo: Reuters
 Boycotting the Grammys or a missed opportunity?
 Shortly afterward, JYP Entertainment confirmed that Stray Kids would not be participating. According to Koreatimes , based on reliable data analysis, no artists from the four major entertainment companies (HYBE, SM, JYP, and YG) have submitted entries for this new category so far. Billboard magazine also revealed that this category has only received 116 entries, a much smaller number compared to other new categories.
 You may also like However, the boycott is not mandatory for the entire industry. HYBE clarified that BTS's actions do not represent the entire corporation, and other artists still have the right to make their own decisions.
 Commenting on the Korea Times , Dr. Kim Hee-yon (Cornell SC Johnson School of Business) suggested that fans might be wrongly blaming the artists. The expert analyzed: BTS is already so famous that they don't need a Grammy to prove their status, but for emerging groups, a Grammy nomination is an incredibly valuable springboard.
 Ms. Kim emphasized that the core responsibility still lies with the organizers. They must prove that the new category truly celebrates Asian artists, rather than becoming a "cage" that traps them.
 The official nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards will be announced on November 16th.
